correctness.rationale: Each degree-two page vertex needs one same-coloured neighbour. With equal spine colours every page must be monochromatic; at least L=floor(b/2) complete pages must share the spine colour because the spine edge already counts. Choose those pages and partition the others by Stirling numbers. For distinct spine colours, the only page types are (X,Y), (X,X), (Y,Y), and (Z,Z) with Z a non-spine colour. If these multiplicities are p,x,y,z, the two spine quotas are p+x,p+y≥H=L+1, so the multinomial chooses all page indices and S(z,k−2) allocates the non-spine pages without dividing by two (spine classes are anchored). The two cases are disjoint. The equal-spine maximum forces exactly L spine-coloured pages and separate classes on all other pages. For distinct spines z≤b−H, and equality in the colour bound forces p+x+y=H and then x=y=0, giving the second extremal type. Pascal's identity gives the total count. Merging classes preserves feasibility, so the spectrum has no holes up to the attainable maximum; k=1 and b=1 are included by the Stirling conventions. Named surjections have exactly k! labellings per partition. Independent finite enumeration checked spectra {1:1,2:2}, {1:1,2:3}, {1:1,2:19,3:6}, and {1:1,2:31,3:10} through b=4, agreeing with the frozen outputs. The frozen script and recorded arithmetic checks through b=20 were inspected, not executed; the proof covers all b.

value.rationale: Square-page books form a natural repeated Cartesian-product family with two high-degree vertices and locally constrained degree-two pages. The exact enumeration separates spine agreement from the coupled two-quota case, gives each coefficient rather than just maximum feasibility, and explains the two extremal types. It is reusable for exact counts on the whole family, not an arbitrary small-instance table.
